v.rationale: All four use the same core pattern: a batch seeded with a fan-out job that adds per-account jobs, with allowFailures and a finally callback. They are separated by bugs found with a real mailer and a real queue. impl-1 imports a non-existent Attachment class, so every account fails in production and no owner email is ever sent (confirmed by probe); the faked-mail tests hide it, so it ranks last. impl-2 is the simplest, but it counts failures only inside a catch with no failed() hook, so timeouts and worker crashes go uncounted and the run can report 'completed'. It also uses string constants instead of an enum, and its finalize step is not idempotent. impl-3 and impl-4 are both modern (enum, #[Scope], queue attributes, atomic idempotent finalize, PDF attachments) and both share the fan-out Tries(3) duplication risk. impl-4 edges ahead: it uses the batch's own failure count, retries per-account jobs with backoff without regenerating PDFs, and has the most realistic tests (a real queue worker, and a check that nothing lands on the default queue). Its weaknesses are the fan-out failure counted as an account failure and deleted accounts skipped silently. None of the four prunes job_batches or failed_jobs.
